scope: Four individually reviewed profiles; not approval of the nationwide candidate queue. No images included pending separate license review. Coordinates remain site-level reference points, not surveyed grave pins.

candidates.name: Gerald Ford
candidates.short_description: 38th U.S. president, Navy veteran, and University of Michigan football standout.
candidates.biography: Gerald Ford became the 38th U.S. president after Richard Nixon resigned in 1974. Raised in Grand Rapids, he played on Michigan's national championship football teams, coached at Yale, and served aboard the USS Monterey during World War II. He later represented western Michigan in Congress. His presidential library's official biography confirms his interment on the grounds of the Gerald R. Ford Presidential Museum in Grand Rapids.
candidates.why_interesting: Before the White House, Ford was Michigan's football MVP and a wartime Navy officer.

burial_evidence.notes: National Archives presidential library biography explicitly confirms interment on the museum grounds in Grand Rapids, not the library in Ann Arbor. Birth and death dates match the candidate. Biography supports presidency, football career, and Navy service. Museum reference point only; not an exact grave or entrance.

candidates.name: Ulysses S. Grant
candidates.short_description: Union commanding general, 18th U.S. president, and author of celebrated military memoirs.
candidates.biography: Ulysses S. Grant rose to command the Union armies during the Civil War and later served two terms as the 18th U.S. president. Near the end of his life, he completed his military memoirs while facing terminal illness and financial losses. The National Park Service identifies General Grant National Memorial in New York City as his resting place. Grant and his wife Julia are entombed there; the map marks the memorial site, not a separate outdoor grave.
candidates.why_interesting: His journey led from West Point to the presidency—and finally to the memoirs he finished shortly before his death.

burial_evidence.notes: The memorial's National Park Service page identifies the mausoleum as the final resting place of Ulysses and Julia Grant. The separate NPS person biography confirms dates, presidency, military command, memoirs, and cemetery name. This is the permanent tomb, not the temporary 1885 tomb. Site-level map reference only.

candidates.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
candidates.burial_place_name: Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt Burial Site
candidates.short_description: 32nd U.S. president who led the country through the New Deal and most of World War II.
candidates.biography: Franklin D. Roosevelt took office during the Great Depression and introduced the New Deal. He became the only American president elected to four terms, leading the country through most of World War II before his death in 1945. Following his instructions, he was buried in the rose garden at Springwood, his family home in Hyde Park, New York. Eleanor Roosevelt was later buried beside him.
candidates.why_interesting: The president's resting place is in the garden of the home where his life began, rather than in Washington.

burial_evidence.notes: NPS's burial-site article confirms Franklin's 1945 burial in the Springwood rose garden and Eleanor's subsequent interment there. NPS's individual biography confirms identity, dates, and presidency. Not the Washington memorial or Warm Springs death site. Coordinates are a site reference, not surveyed grave precision.

candidates.name: Eleanor Roosevelt
candidates.burial_place_name: Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt Burial Site
candidates.short_description: First lady, writer, and advocate for civil and human rights.
candidates.biography: Eleanor Roosevelt built a public career as a writer, speaker, and advocate for civil and human rights. As first lady, she traveled widely and drew attention to people whose concerns often went unheard. Her work continued after Franklin Roosevelt's death, including service at the United Nations. She died in 1962 and was buried beside Franklin in the rose garden at Springwood in Hyde Park, New York.
candidates.why_interesting: Her public work extended well beyond the White House, into journalism and international human rights.

burial_evidence.notes: NPS explicitly confirms Eleanor's interment beside Franklin in 1962. NPS person biography confirms dates and rose garden location. Resolved the collector's broader Home of FDR site to the same shared burial-site entity used for Franklin. No separate grave pin claimed.
